summary: toString() sets the text println shows for your object, and equals() decides when two objects hold the same data. In Java, == on objects only checks if they are the same object.
notes: When you override equals(), also override hashCode(), or HashSet and HashMap will not find matching objects.
equals(Object other) checks instanceof first, so a.equals(1001) returns false instead of throwing ClassCastException.
roster.contains(b) calls equals() on each item, so it finds a matching Student by id.
pitfall: Writing public boolean equals(Student other) overloads instead of overrides, so contains() and HashSet still use the default identity check. With @Override the compiler reports "method does not override or implement a method from a supertype".
